title: The whole icon workflow runs start to finish in one walk at Next defaults
goal: Every step of making an icon has been proved on its own, but nothing has yet gone from an empty window to a moving SVG in one go, and the focus says it must be walked end to end. Doing it once, the way a person would, shows what still trips someone up between the steps.
notes: Found in the digest of 2026-11-07. The focus in queue/objectives.json names the workflow: start a 24 unit icon, keylines and snapping on, draw a cloud-download glyph from shapes and the Pen, union it, give it a 1.75 round stroke, check it at 16, 24 and 48, make it swing or spin forever, export an animated SVG for a web page. No walk under Scripts/playtest does more than a part of this (grep for cloud finds only opening-an-svg-walk and border-follows-the-shape-walk). Stepping along the first half by hand found the typed Width fault at once, so expect more. While walking, judge the panel too: a rectangle in an icon frame shows Columns and Layout sections that say little about an icon (queue/audits/2026-11-07-icon-place-tag-1-box-sc.png, and the same on 2026-11-06). Seen twice now. If it gets in the way, say so in the audit. Each fault this finds that is not a one line fix gets its own task; do not fold them all in here.
acceptance: One walk at Next defaults with no flags does every step of the focus workflow, on File, New, Image, Icon and again on a 24 unit frame, through pointer clicks and keys, and exports an animated SVG
The exported SVG is opened in a browser and plays, and the audit says so with a picture
The audit lists every step that was clumsy, surprising or took a second try, as a person trying it would see them, with a picture for each
Any step that fails either passes before this closes or has its own open task named in the audit
